newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas holds late gains on charts, cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas holds late gains on charts, cash.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natural gas futures held gains late Wednesday in fairly active trade, still underpinned by technical buying and short covering amid reports of notionally firmer cash prices, sources said.
At 1405 EDT, May was still up by 5.3 cents at $2.195 per million British thermal units, while June was four cents higher at $2.205. Other months remained up by 0.8 to 3.3 cents.

"I think this is mostly a technical rally. The funds have been big buyers. Cash is up but it's following, not leading," said one Texas-based trader, noting 6-10 day forecasts for hotter weather in Texas that should stir some cooling loads.

And while storage remains well-above last year's record lows, some noted current levels lagged the average for the last three years, raising the prospect for steady injection demand at least early in the season.
A Reuter poll showed most expected a 10-25 bcf weekly gas stock build when AGA data are released later today. Last year at this time, overall inventories gained 68 bcf.
But most agreed it would take a broader heat wave, one that hits the Midwest and Northeast, to drive prices much higher.
"I think prices will stay relatively strong into summer, but I don't see them running up too much from here," a Texas producer said.

Technical traders said June's break this morning above resistance at $2.18 should lead to a test of next resistance in the $2.24 area. Further selling should emerge ahead of the $2.385 contract high. June support was seen at $2.05 and then along the up trendline in the $2.01 area.

In the May cash, Gulf Coast prices notionally were talked more than a nickel higher Wednesday in the $2.10-15 range. Midcon pipes were up a few cents to the mid-to-high $1.90s. New York city gate gas also was modestly higher at about $2.40.
NYMEX said 36,138 contracts traded at 1330 EDT.
On the KCBT, June was still five cents higher at $2.03, while deferreds were steady to four cents higher. The East/West spread widened by 0.3 cent to 16.5 cents (NYMEX premium).
